stack_detection.method: bundle id; AX answers with labeled content on first query

channel_setup: Accessibility TCC only. Read-only probe (no clicks, no typing) — the app was probed as the campaign's prime custom-drawn silent-divergence suspect.

t1_read_text.detail: Rich labeled content: 'Rechercher (⌘E)', account button 'Zoom, Léandre Carpentier, Connecté…', navigation tabs with selection state ('Accueil, selected, 1 of 6', 'Réunions, 3 of 6').

t2_enumerate.detail: 42 AXButtons + links + popups with frames. Nav tabs use role AXUnknown yet still carry full descriptive labels and selection state — role-agnostic readers keep working.

t3_live_value.detail: Read-only cell by design (user's real account).

t4_living_screen.detail: Not tested (no meeting; the in-meeting video canvas is the real pictorial test and was out of scope on a live account).

t6_pictorial.detail: Home window has no video canvas. The in-meeting surface remains THE open question for Zoom; untested here, honestly deferred.

measurements.notes: The 'custom-drawn Electron-ish suspect' did NOT materialize on the home window: Zoom ships thorough AX annotations (three embedded WebAreas + native controls, all labeled, tab indices included). 55–103 nodes / 6.8 KB / 17 ms. A second small promo window exposed only 2 nodes ('Travaillez plus vite avec Zoom Workplace') — thin but honest. Verdict scope: home window only; in-meeting screen-share/video surfaces are expected to be declared-opaque at best and were not probed.

runtime_verification.method: Labels cross-checked against the visible home window state (logged-in account name, selected tab).
